title: Buffers, bytes and encodings
summary: Buffer as Node's byte array, text encodings, base64, and slicing and copying without surprises.

sections.title: Bytes, not strings
sections.body:
Network and file data arrive as **bytes**. Node represents them with `Buffer`, a subclass of `Uint8Array`. A string is converted with an **encoding**: `Buffer.from('héllo', 'utf8')` is 6 bytes because `é` takes two bytes in UTF-8, while `'héllo'.length` is 5 UTF-16 code units.

Common encodings: `utf8` (default), `base64` and `base64url`, `hex`, `latin1`. The browser-standard `TextEncoder` and `TextDecoder` work in Node too.
sections.code:
const b = Buffer.from('héllo')
b.length            // 6 bytes
b.toString('hex')   // '68c3a96c6c6f'
b.toString('base64') // 'aMOpbGxv'
Buffer.byteLength('héllo') // 6

sections.title: Slices share memory
sections.body:
`buf.subarray(start, end)` (and the older `slice`) returns a **view** of the same memory, so writing to the view changes the original. Use `Buffer.from(view)` or `Buffer.copyBytesFrom` when you need an independent copy.

`Buffer.alloc(n)` gives zero-filled memory. `Buffer.allocUnsafe(n)` is faster but may contain old data from the pool; only use it when you overwrite every byte before reading.

sections.title: Decoding chunked text
sections.body: A multi-byte character can be split across two chunks. Calling `chunk.toString()` on each chunk then produces replacement characters. Use `TextDecoder` with `{ stream: true }`, `StringDecoder`, or `setEncoding('utf8')` on a readable, which all keep the partial bytes for the next chunk.

pitfalls: Using `string.length` where the byte length matters, such as in a `Content-Length` header.
Decoding each chunk separately and corrupting multi-byte characters.
Mutating a `subarray` view and accidentally changing the original buffer.

gotchas.question: How much bigger is base64 than the original bytes?
gotchas.answer: About 4/3: every 3 bytes become 4 characters, plus `=` padding to a multiple of 4. 1 MB of binary becomes about 1.33 MB of base64.

gotchas.question: What is the difference between `base64` and `base64url`?
gotchas.answer: `base64url` replaces `+` with `-` and `/` with `_` and usually drops the `=` padding, so the result is safe in URLs and file names. JWT segments use it.

gotchas.question: Why is comparing secrets with `===` risky?
gotchas.answer: String comparison can return as soon as one character differs, so response timing leaks how much of a guess was right. Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on two buffers of equal length.
